description:
Edit repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/gap-to-feature.ts. ONE contiguous string replacement in that ONE file.

A gap whose escalation a human has answered receives a bounded exemption from the hopeless() category seal, but nothing in selection priority — so it gets one attempt and then loses the queue to gaps with 60-120 failed attempts. Measured 2026-08-29: the lift-gate gap had 2 of 3 exemption attempts unspent and was picked ZERO times in 25 minutes, while three competitors with failed_attempts of 122, 82 and 64 were each picked 8 times. The operator's answer is the substrate's most expensive input and it currently buys one attempt.

The impact term already exists in the picker and already has a precedent for exactly this: human_reported gaps are treated preferentially. Find the scoring expression that computes impactOf / the score used in the `[gap-to-feature] pick` log (it emits landability, impact and score), and give a gap with classification_metadata.human_exemption_attempts_remaining > 0 the SAME kind of preference the human_reported flag already receives, so its remaining exemption attempts are actually consumed rather than stranded.

DO NOT zero or reset failed_attempts to achieve this. That is the already-filed and closed narrowing defect (narrowing-a-chronically-stuck-gap-copies-it-verbatim-and-only-resets-the-penalty): a child gap copied verbatim with failed_attempts:0 outranks its own parent forever. The exemption must raise selection priority WITHOUT falsifying the gap's attempt history.

Keep the exemption bounded: this changes only priority while human_exemption_attempts_remaining > 0, and bumpFailedAttempts already decrements that counter on every non-landing attempt, so the preference expires on its own.

The change must typecheck. VERIFY BY CONSEQUENCE: a gap carrying a human exemption consumes all 3 of its attempts within a bounded window instead of stalling at 1, and its failed_attempts continues to increment normally.
